'''Michinooku no Kikuta no Kuni no Miyatsuko''' (道奥菊多国造) was a {{ill|Kuni no miyatsuko|es|Kuni no miyatsuko|ff|Kuni no miyatsuko|it|Kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造|ko|국조 (일본)|simple|Kuni no miyatsuko|vi|Kuni no miyatsuko|zh|國造|qid=Q2483673|lt=Kuni no Miyatsuko}}, or regional governor, said to have governed the region of {{ill|Michinoku Kikuta Kuni-no-Miyatsuko|ja|道奥菊多国造|qid=Q11641674}}.

The domain of this Kuni no Miyatsuko is believed to have corresponded to the later {{ill|Kikuta district|ja|菊多郡|qid=Q11619613}}, an area centered in the southern part of what is now {{ill|Iwaki, Fukushima|ar|لواكي (فوكوشيما)|arz|لواكى|azb|ایواکی، فوکوشیما|bg|Иваки|ca|Iwaki|ce|Иваки (Фукусима)|ceb|Iwaki-shi|de|Iwaki|eo|Iwaki|es|Iwaki (Fukushima)|eu|Iwaki (Fukushima)|fa|ایواکی، فوکوشیما|fi|Iwaki|fr|Iwaki|ga|Iwaki|gl|Iwaki|hu|Ivaki (Fukusima)|hy|Իվակի|id|Iwaki, Fukushima|is|Iwaki|it|Iwaki|ja|いわき市|kk|Иваки|ko|이와키시|lt|Ivakis|mg|Iwaki|mzn|ایواکی، فوکوشیما|nl|Iwaki (Fukushima)|no|Iwaki|pl|Iwaki|pt|Iwaki|ro|Iwaki|ru|Иваки (город)|sh|Ivaki|simple|Iwaki, Fukushima|sr|Иваки|sv|Iwaki|tg|Иваки|th|อิวากิ (จังหวัดฟูกูชิมะ)|tl|Iwaki, Fukushima|tr|Iwaki, Fukuşima|tt|Иваки (Фукусима)|uk|Івакі (Фукусіма)|ur|ایواکی، فوکوشیما|uz|Ivaki(Iwaki), Fukushima|vi|Iwaki, Fukushima|war|Iwaki, Fukushima|za|Banjsingz Si|zh|磐城市|zh_classical|磐城市|zh_min_nan|Iwaki-chhī|zh_yue|磐城|qid=Q274384|lt=Iwaki, Fukushima}}, Fukushima Prefecture. Later, it became part of {{ill|takanokunimiyatsuko|ja|高国造|qid=Q11668988}}, which stretched from {{ill|Sukegawa|ja|助川}} to {{ill|kumakawa|ja|熊川|ko|웅천|zh|熊川|qid=Q11567884}}. During the establishment of the {{ill|Ritsuryō|en|Ritsuryō|qid=Q742460|lt=Ritsuryō system}}, the region was initially incorporated into {{ill|Hitachi Province|cs|Provincie Hitači|de|Provinz Hitachi|es|Provincia de Hitachi|fa|ولایت هیتاچی|fr|Province de Hitachi|gl|Provincia de Hitachi|hak|Hitachi-koet|id|Provinsi Hitachi|it|Hitachi (provincia)|ja|常陸国|ko|히타치국|lt|Hitačio žemė|nl|Hitachi (provincie)|pt|Província de Hitachi|ru|Хитати (провинция)|simple|Hitachi Province|sk|Hitači (provincia)|sr|Провинција Хитачи|tr|Hitachi (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Хітаті|zh|常陸國|zh_min_nan|Hitati-kok|zh_yue|常陸國|qid=Q1055353|lt=Hitachi Province}}, with its northern boundary marked by "Kuma" (Kumagawa).<ref>''Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei: Fukushima no Chimei,'' p. 205.</ref> Subsequently, it was reassigned to {{ill|Mutsu Province|ca|Província de Mutsu|cs|Provincie Mucu|de|Provinz Mutsu|es|Provincia de Mutsu|fa|ولایت موتسو|fi|Mutsun provinssi|fr|Province de Mutsu|gl|Provincia de Mutsu|id|Provinsi Mutsu|it|Mutsu (provincia)|ja|陸奥国|ko|무쓰국|lt|Mucu žemė|nl|Mutsu (provincie)|pt|Província de Mutsu|ru|Муцу (провинция)|simple|Mutsu Province|sk|Mucu (provincia)|sr|Провинција Муцу|tr|Mutsu (vilayet)|uk|Муцу (провінція)|zh|陸奧國|zh_classical|陸奧國|zh_min_nan|Mutu-kok|zh_yue|陸奧國|qid=Q907389|lt=Mutsu Province}}. Due to this historical trajectory, the area was regarded as the northernmost territory under the control of the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|en|Yamato Kingship|qid=Q2658252|lt=Yamato court}} before its northern expansion and was said to host {{ill|Kikuta Seki|ja|菊多関}}, a precursor to the more famous {{ill|Nakoso no seki|ja|勿来関|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakoso Barrier|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11400650}}. 

== Ancestry ==
According to the "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi" chapter of the {{ill|Kujiki|en|Kujiki|qid=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kuji Hongi}}, the position of Kuni no Miyatsuko originated during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|en|Emperor Ōjin|qid=Q317997|lt=Emperor Ōjin}} when '''Yashiro Tōne''', a son of {{ill|Takekoro-no-Mikoto|ja|建許侶命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takekuro no Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 建許呂命|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11486843}}, the ancestor of the {{ill|Q11617300|ja|茨城国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ibaraki Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11617300}}, was appointed as the first Kuni no Miyatsuko.

== Clan ==
The {{ill|hasetsukabeuji|ja|丈部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hasebe clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q55530004}} (はせつかべうじ, kabane unknown) was associated with the Kikuta no Miyatsuko. In the 12th year of the {{ill|Zhenguan|en|Zhenguan|qid=Q3577278|lt=Jōgan era}} (870 CE), members of the Kikuta District, including Hasebe Tsugimaro and Hasebe Hamanari, were granted the surname of {{ill|Yumoriza Kikuta no Omi|ja|湯坐菊多臣}}. Other related families include the Yumoriza Hiratsune no Ren and the Munewakabe clan.

== Shrine ==
* {{ill|Kunitama|ja|國魂神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kunitama Shrine (Iwaki)|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 国魂|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q9692242}} – Located in Kuboita, Motonaka-chō, Iwaki City, Fukushima Prefecture, this shrine is said to have been founded by the Kikuta no Miyatsuko.
